public_rationale: OpenAI's GPT-4 technical report came out about two weeks before the post. It says outright that it 'contains no further details about the architecture (including model size), hardware, training compute, dataset construction, training method, or similar.' What it did disclose was generic: a 'Transformer-style' model, trained on public and licensed data, then fine-tuned with RLHF. Marcus raised the point to ask how anyone could tell whether a system is more powerful than GPT-4. Read plainly in that context, 'no details' means no substantive specifics such as size, structure, or dataset makeup. OpenAI's own statement confirms that. Read word for word, 'no details' overstates things, because a few one-line labels were published. I treat that as hyperbole, not as a factual error.
limitations: The result depends on reading 'no details' as 'no substantive details'. A strictly literal reading would make the claim partly false, because a few generic facts were disclosed (e2).
I did not review every informal OpenAI statement from the period.

our_interpretation: Read as: by 2023-03-29, OpenAI had not published substantive technical details of GPT-4's architecture (such as model size or structure) or of its training data (such as dataset makeup or construction).

The context is his question about how anyone could tell whether a system is 'more powerful than GPT-4'. So the details that matter are the specific ones (size, compute, data makeup), not one-line generic labels.

One-line generic descriptions such as 'Transformer-style' or 'public and licensed data' are not counted as 'details' under this plain reading. A strictly literal reading would count them, and would make the claim overstated.
criteria.support_condition: OpenAI's public GPT-4 materials up to 2023-03-29 withheld specific architecture details (size, structure, compute) and specific training-data details (sources, makeup, construction).
criteria.contradiction_condition: By 2023-03-29, OpenAI or another authoritative source had published substantive specifics of GPT-4's architecture or training dataset, such as parameter count, layer structure, or dataset makeup.
